definitions.explanation: The upper limb of the body from shoulder to hand.
One's ability or skill at something, especially a craft or profession.

examples.japanese: {腕|うで}を{上|あ}げてください。
{腕|うで}{時計|どけい}をしています。
{右|みぎ}{腕|うで}が{痛|いた}くて{動|うご}かせません。
examples.english: My right arm hurts and I can't move it.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{腕|うで}に{抱|だ}いて、ゆっくりと{歩|ある}きました。
examples.english: Holding the child in my arms, I walked slowly.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{料理|りょうり}の{腕|うで}がいい。
{腕|うで}を{磨|みが}くために{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}する。
examples.english: I practice every day to improve my skills.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{仕事|しごと}の{腕|うで}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.english: That person has excellent work skills.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はピアノの{腕|うで}を{上|あ}げるために、{毎日|まいにち}{三|さん}{時間|じかん}{練習|れんしゅう}しています。
examples.english: She practices three hours every day to improve her piano skills.

notes: {腕|うで} refers to the entire arm, not just a part of it. It's also commonly used to mean 'skill' or 'ability,' especially in contexts of craftsmanship: {腕|うで}がいい (skilled), {腕|うで}を{磨|みが}く (to improve one's skills). {腕|うで}{時計|どけい} is a wristwatch, {腕|うで}{組|ぐ}み is folding one's arms.
